extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, funders, information innovators, policymakers, ethicists, journalists and others involved in reporting and publication of scientific research
extracted.subtask_description: Call for abstracts for the Ninth International Congress on Peer Review and Scientific Publication (September 2022). Authors should prepare submissions relevant to research on peer review and scientific publication, mindful of the conference timeline and multidisciplinary audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timeline / deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The website will open for abstracts submissions on December 1, 2021. The deadline for abstract submissions will be January 31, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit abstracts only during the submission window; check the Congress website for submission forms and any additional timing/format details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope: peer review and scientific publication research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Congress has helped stimulate research into peer review and scientific publication — including studies of bias, reporting standards, prospective registration and many more topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts should address aspects of peer review and scientific publication (examples given: bias, reporting standards, prospective registration). Use the Congress website or editorial for a fuller list of acceptable topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary relevance / cross-disciplinary sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Congress now embraces a wide range of disciplines. Sharing findings and experimentation across disciplinary boundaries is particularly important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that is relevant beyond a single discipline, or that demonstrates lessons transferable across fields, is especially encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience relevance / stakeholder applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience includes researchers, editors, funders, information innovators, policymakers, ethicists, journalists and more — i.e., all those who participate in the reporting and publication of scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design abstracts and presentations with this diverse audience in mind; emphasize implications for multiple stakeholders when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based contributions to improve peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers aim to assemble a stimulating program of evidence-based discussions to improve the quality, effectiveness and fairness of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts should ideally present empirical evidence, rigorous evaluation, or well-documented experimentation that can inform improvements in peer-review quality, effectiveness, or fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check organizers for specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: You can watch the virtual symposium if you want to hear specifics from organizers of the Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For detailed submission requirements, formatting, evaluation criteria, and other guidance beyond this announcement, consult the Congress website, the co-published editorial (JAMA and BMJ), or organizer-provided materials/sessions.
